=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of the Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Preliminary point: the "[STANDARD]" labels and "Reviewer Efficiency Note"

The Seller's note says clauses marked [STANDARD] "have been reviewed and cleared by both sides". It also says the Buyer has "already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package". **We should not proceed on that basis.**

- The labels and the note are the Seller's own characterisation, inside the Seller's own draft.
- Almost every substantive position is labelled [STANDARD], including the ones most adverse to us.
- Nothing in what I've seen shows the Buyer agreed to any of it.

Unless the deal team has a signed term sheet or email recording that agreement, I have reviewed every position on its merits. **Please confirm with the deal lead that nothing here was conceded.** We should also tell Seller counsel in writing that the package remains open in full. Otherwise silence could later be portrayed as acceptance.

The Disclosure Letter itself is more candid than the cover note. It confirms that Bluefen consent, the Riverlark discharge, the Ironquay payment and assignment, and the DD-006 investigation are all **unresolved**. The cover note presents them as handled.

---

## A. Limitation regime

### 1. Fundamental warranties folded into the general cap and time limit (High)
The Seller proposes that title and capacity warranties sit under the AUD 4.8m cap, the 18-month limit and the thresholds, "for administrative simplicity". That is not market. If title fails, we lose the whole AUD 24m but could recover at most AUD 4.8m.

**Push back:**
- Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, solvency, share capital) should be capped at **100% of the price**.
- They should run for **at least 5–7 years**, or the statutory limitation period.
- They should sit **outside the de minimis and basket**.

### 2. "Limitations apply to all Claims of any nature" (cl 12.3/13, 9.3/12.8/20.5) (High)
As drafted, this would cap and time-bar fraud, specific indemnities, the tax indemnity and fundamental warranties.

**Push back:**
- Carve out **fraud, dishonesty and wilful concealment** from all limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions.
- Specific indemnities and the tax indemnity should have their own caps and time limits, and sit outside the de minimis and basket.
- Non-reliance should not purport to exclude the Seller's liability for the Warranties and Disclosure Letter. It should be limited so far as the law permits. Misleading-conduct liability under the Australian Consumer Law cannot be fully contracted out of in any event.

### 3. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime" (High)
A 20% cap and 18-month limit for tax is inadequate given ATO amendment periods.

**Push back:**
- A separate **tax indemnity/covenant**, capped at 100% of the price, running at least 4–5 years (or ATO amendment period plus 60–90 days).
- The tax indemnity should be first-dollar.
- IP warranties should run at least 3 years. A cap above the general cap is justified given the Ironquay issue (item 8).

### 4. Cap, thresholds and general time limit (Medium)
- **Cap:** 20% (AUD 4.8m) is within the market range only if W&I insurance sits above it. Without W&I, seek 30–50%. **Please confirm whether W&I is being placed.**
- **Basket:** AUD 250k (about 1%) is within market. Seek a **tipping basket** (recover from the first dollar once it is exceeded), not a deductible.
- **De minimis:** AUD 25k is fairly high for a business of this size. Seek AUD 10–15k, with related claims aggregated.
- **Time limit:** 18 months is acceptable but low. Seek 24 months, covering two audit cycles.

---

## B. Disclosure framework

### 5. General disclosure of the whole data room and public registers (Schedule 7; DL 1.1–1.2) (High)
Disclosing "every fact… contained or referred to" in the entire data room, plus public records, would qualify the warranties against anything buried anywhere. Combined with item 6, this leaves very little warranty protection.

**Push back:**
- Specific disclosure only, against identified warranties.
- Each disclosure must be **"fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter"**.
- At most, allow a limited general disclosure of an agreed, indexed data room, subject to the same fair-disclosure standard. No disclosure of "referred to" documents, and no blanket disclosure of public records beyond searches of specified registers on specified dates.
- Disclosures must **not qualify the specific indemnities or the tax indemnity**.

### 6. Buyer knowledge / anti-sandbagging (cl 8.3) (High)
This clause covers the knowledge of the Buyer *and its advisers*, plus anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records. That is constructive knowledge at its broadest. Seller-side W&I insurers would not require it.

**Push back:**
- Delete it and replace it with a **pro-sandbagging clause**: Buyer knowledge, actual or constructive, does not reduce claims except to the extent fairly disclosed.
- Fallback: actual knowledge of named individuals, of the specific breach, before signing.

### 7. DL 1.4 non-admission (Low)
This is acceptable as drafted. Make sure it cannot be read as negating the facts disclosed. The disclosures, notably DL 2–6, should be treated as statements the Seller warrants are accurate.

---

## C. Specific transaction risks

### 8. Ironquay SOW3 IP (cl 11.1; DD-004, DD-010) (High)
Under DD-004 cl 7.3, ownership of the SOW3 Project Materials transfers only on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. AUD 180k remains open, with no receipt and no confirmatory assignment. **The Company may not own IP it depends on.** An indemnity limited to "the specific SOW3 payment" covers the debt but not the real risk: loss of ownership, third-party infringement claims, or Ironquay withholding the materials.

**Push back:**
- **Completion deliverables:** evidence of cleared payment, funded by the Seller or deducted from price, plus an executed **confirmatory IP assignment deed** from Ironquay.
- Broaden the indemnity to all Loss arising from the Company not owning, or being unable to use, the SOW3 materials. It should sit outside the general cap and basket and have a minimum 3–5 year term.

### 9. DD-006 export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6) (High)
About 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) were sent to an unintended external address. Whether anyone accessed them is unknown. The investigation is still "preliminary" more than six weeks after the 22 September disclosure date. Under the Privacy Act Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, an entity must assess a suspected eligible data breach within 30 days, so **the assessment may already be overdue**. That creates regulatory exposure in itself, on top of any notification failure. The Seller calling this "not expected to be material" is an assertion, and the Disclosure Letter does not support it.

**Push back:**
- **Before Completion:** a completed incident assessment, the forensic or IT findings, a documented NDB decision (including any OAIC and individual notifications), and evidence that the link was revoked and the file deleted or recovered.
- A **specific indemnity** for all Loss from the incident: regulatory penalties, notification and remediation costs, claims, and investigation costs. It should be first-dollar, outside the general cap (separate cap or price-level), and unaffected by disclosure or Buyer knowledge. W&I will exclude this known matter, so the indemnity is our only protection.
- A pre-Completion covenant to manage the incident in consultation with the Buyer.
- Consider a retention or escrow sized to the exposure.

### 10. Bluefen change-control consent (cl 3 / 6.3; DD-002) (High)
Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue (around AUD 3.6m). No final consent exists, and the clause 11.3 conditions are unsatisfied. The Seller offers only "reasonable endeavours" and would treat the condition as satisfied on mere delivery of a written consent. That would be satisfied even if the consent is conditional or onerous, or if the 11.3 conditions remain unmet.

**Push back:**
- A **condition precedent**: Bluefen's written, unconditional consent (or consent on terms acceptable to the Buyer acting reasonably), with all cl 11.3 conditions satisfied, and no amendment to pricing, term or termination rights.
- **"All reasonable endeavours"** from the Seller, with the Buyer involved in Bluefen communications.
- The CP is for the Buyer's benefit and waivable only by the Buyer, with a sunset date and a walk right.
- Consider a price adjustment or earn-out mechanism if Bluefen terminates or materially changes terms within 12 months of Completion.

### 11. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7; DD-003) (High)
This is a debt-free/cash-free deal, and AUD 3.2m is outstanding. The facility has a change-control clause (8.1), so **Completion itself may trigger default**. A "release to be provided following Completion" leaves the Company, and therefore us, holding the debt and security risk.

**Push back:**
- A Riverlark **payout letter** before Completion stating the exact payout figure and daily interest.
- The payout amount is **deducted from the price** and paid directly to Riverlark from the Completion funds flow.
- A **deed of release and discharge**, plus PPSR financing-change-statement releases (or undertakings to lodge within 1–2 business days) as Completion deliverables.
- Riverlark debt, break costs and fees must fall within Net Debt.

### 12. Employee Completion bonuses of AUD 420k (funds flow; DD-005) (High)
The Seller says these are "a matter for the Seller" yet they are absent from the funds flow. The Company is the employer, so the Company, which we will own, bears the obligation along with PAYG withholding, any payroll tax and potentially superannuation and on-costs. The Seller has not addressed on-costs at all.

**Push back:**
- Treat the bonuses **plus all on-costs** (payroll tax, superannuation where applicable, workers' compensation, and the employer share of any taxes) as **Debt or a Transaction Expense**, deducted from the price.
- Pay them through Company payroll with correct withholding, funded by the Seller.
- Add a specific indemnity for any shortfall or related claims, including amounts paid to employees who leave or fail the conditions.
- Check for any other change-of-control payments and require a warranty that none exist.

### 13. Sandbar renewals, AUD 330k (DD-008, DD-011) (Medium–High)
These are three "related" renewals of exactly AUD 110k each, which DL 8 itself says should be read together. That pattern suggests a single commitment **split to stay under an approval or materiality threshold**, for example in the conduct-of-business covenant or a material contracts warranty. The Seller's "ordinary course" label is unsupported, and the Disclosure Letter declines to say whether the contracts are terminable or accrued.

**Push back:**
- Obtain the contracts and confirm timing, terms and terminability.
- If they were entered into after the locked-box or signing date, or without Buyer consent where it was needed, require the Seller to bear the cost, unwind them, or treat them as leakage or debt.
- Add **aggregation language** to the conduct-of-business and material-contract thresholds so that related transactions count together.
- Add a warranty that they are on arm's-length, ordinary-course terms.

### 14. Title evidence (DD-012) (High)
A share register alone is not sufficient evidence of title.

**Push back:**
- Reconcile the register against an ASIC company extract.
- Require original or lost-certificate indemnities for share certificates, and a PPSR search against the Seller to confirm the shares are unencumbered.
- Require constitutional pre-emption waivers and board approval of the transfer.
- Title is warranted on a fundamental basis (see item 1).

### 15. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009) (Low–Medium)
The disclosures say no consent is needed for a share sale. **We should verify this ourselves.** Check the lease and the Mossvale agreement for change-of-control clauses that deem a change of control to be an assignment.
- The lease notification should become a Completion step or covenant.
- Add a warranty that no material contract is triggered by the transaction other than those listed.

---

## D. Funds flow and price mechanics

The funds flow reportedly "reflects the agreed price mechanics", yet it omits both Riverlark and the bonuses. Before signing:
- Agree Debt, Debt-Like Items and Transaction Expenses definitions that expressly include the Riverlark payout, the bonuses and their on-costs, the Ironquay arrears (if the Company pays them), and Seller advisers' fees.
- Confirm whether the deal uses a locked box (in which case we need leakage protection that covers the bonuses and Sandbar) or completion accounts.

---

## Summary of Recommendations

| # | Issue | Priority | Buyer position |
|---|---|---|---|
| — | "[STANDARD]/cleared" labelling | High | Reject; confirm in writing that all points remain open |
| 1 | Fundamental warranties under general cap/time | High | 100% cap, 5–7 yrs, outside thresholds |
| 2 | Limitations apply to all Claims | High | Carve out fraud; separate regimes for indemnities and tax |
| 3 | Tax/IP under general regime | High | Tax indemnity at 100%, ATO period+; longer IP survival |
| 4 | Cap/basket/de minimis/time | Medium | Tipping basket; de minimis AUD 10–15k; 24 months; cap depends on W&I |
| 5 | General disclosure of data room/public records | High | Specific, fair disclosure only; no qualification of indemnities |
| 6 | Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3) | High | Delete; pro-sandbagging |
| 8 | Ironquay SOW3 IP | High | Payment plus confirmatory assignment at Completion; broad indemnity |
| 9 | DD-006 privacy incident | High | Completed assessment/NDB decision pre-Completion; uncapped-style specific indemnity; consider escrow |
| 10 | Bluefen consent (30% revenue) | High | Hard CP: unconditional consent, cl 11.3 satisfied; all reasonable endeavours; Buyer-waivable |
| 11 | Riverlark AUD 3.2m | High | Payout from price at Completion; deed of release and PPSR discharge as deliverables |
| 12 | Bonuses AUD 420k + on-costs | High | Debt-like deduction; payroll processing; indemnity |
| 13 | Sandbar AUD 330k split renewals | Med–High | Diligence; leakage/debt treatment; anti-splitting aggregation |
| 14 | Title (register only) | High | ASIC, PPSR and certificates; fundamental warranty |
| 15 | Lease / Mossvale | Low–Med | Verify independently; completion notification; no-trigger warranty |

**Next steps:**
1. Confirm with the deal lead that no part of the limitation or disclosure package was agreed.
2. Confirm the W&I position.
3. Obtain the full SPA text for clauses 2, 3, 6–9, 11–13 and 20 and Schedules 6–7. My analysis is based on the Seller's summary, not the operative drafting.
4. Request the Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006 and Sandbar documents in full.
5. Prepare a mark-up and issues list on the positions above.

These are issues for review by the supervising lawyers on the deal team, not final legal advice.

- Treat the bonuses **plus all on-costs** (payroll tax, superannuation where applicable, workers' compensation, and the employer share of any taxes) as **Debt or a Transaction Expense**, deducted from the price.
- Pay them through Company payroll with correct withholding, funded by the Seller.
- Add a specific indemnity for any shortfall or related claims, including amounts paid to employees who leave or fail the conditions.
- Check for any other change-of-control payments and require a warranty that none exist.

### 13. Sandbar renewals, AUD 330k (DD-008, DD-011) (Medium–High)
These are three "related" renewals of exactly AUD 110k each, which DL 8 itself says should be read together. That pattern suggests a single commitment **split to stay under an approval or materiality threshold**, for example in the conduct-of-business covenant or a material contracts warranty. The Seller's "ordinary course" label is unsupported, and the Disclosure Letter declines to say whether the contracts are terminable or accrued.

**Push back:**
- Obtain the contracts and confirm timing, terms and terminability.
- If they were entered into after the locked-box or signing date, or without Buyer consent where it was needed, require the Seller to bear the cost, unwind them, or treat them as leakage or debt.
- Add **aggregation language** to the conduct-of-business and material-contract thresholds so that related transactions count together.
- Add a warranty that they are on arm's-length, ordinary-course terms.

### 14. Title evidence (DD-012) (High)
A share register alone is not sufficient evidence of title.

**Push back:**
- Reconcile the register against an ASIC company extract.
- Require original or lost-certificate indemnities for share certificates, and a PPSR search against the Seller to confirm the shares are unencumbered.
- Require constitutional pre-emption waivers and board approval of the transfer.
- Title is warranted on a fundamental basis (see item 1).

### 15. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009) (Low–Medium)
The disclosures say no consent is needed for a share sale. **We should verify this ourselves.** Check the lease and the Mossvale agreement for change-of-control clauses that deem a change of control to be an assignment.
- The lease notification should become a Completion step or covenant.
- Add a warranty that no material contract is triggered by the transaction other than those listed.
